brief: Goldman's morning update leads with the AI capex debate: it argues the profit levels needed to justify current hyperscaler AI spending are achievable sooner than skeptics think, so GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL and SPCX can outperform from here. The chain: the six hyperscalers must generate a combined ~$1.42tn of cumulative CY2028-30 revenue to hit a 15% ROIC on capex, and cloud backlogs of $1.69tn across three companies (+152% YoY) support that monetization path, so near-term return compression reflects the investment cycle rather than broken AI economics. Two caveats qualify the bullish read: hyperscaler capex growth should decelerate to just under 40% in 2027 from 54% in 2026 on financing needs and supply bottlenecks, and the application layer separately needs over $1tn of revenue, raising doubts about 2028 capex levels. Semis multiples already imply an earnings decline, which Goldman calls typical late-cycle behavior, and AI infrastructure stocks trade at a 22X P/E reflecting market skepticism. Separately, France's borrowing-cost gap to Germany is widening, and GS previews today's US durable goods and University of Michigan data, forecasting several components below consensus.
